correctness.rationale: Exact cap area coordinates give heights uniform on [-h,1] and independent uniform azimuths. The angular enclosing simplex has unconditional density 1/(2pi^2). Signed conic pole inclusion is equivalent to sum_i sin(b_i) z_i/sqrt(1-z_i^2)>0. On the bulk region min sin(b_i)>=h^gamma the excluded volume is h^3(sum a_i)^3/(6 product a_i)(1+o(1)); all three angular edges produce aggregate 8 gamma log(1/h). Thin gaps have bounded remainder O(h^3[(1-gamma)log(1/h)+1]); the limit after gamma->1 is 4/pi^2. Sign-partitioned edge integrals split two-southern vs one-southern mass 3:1; logarithmic bands and edge symmetry yield independent marks. Cartesian sample and independent Sobol quadrature agree numerically but are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The hemisphere threshold is geometrically motivated by geodesic convexity and pole containment. The striking leading h^3 log(1/h), not a routine Taylor correction, derives from rare near-semicircular azimuth gaps; the exact 4/pi^2 coefficient and 3:1 sign-mechanism split reveal the structure of the phase transition. This supplies a natural sharp boundary law for a fixed-pole random spherical convex hull.
